podcast.title: Jack Irons' Drumming Role – Early Member
podcast.body: Jack Irons, who later joined the Red Hot Chili Peppers and worked with Pearl Jam, was a drummer for Eleven at one point. His connections to the Seattle music scene further highlight the interconnectedness of many of the era's bands. "There Elaine and a friend named Natasha Schneider formed a group called Eleven, which at one point had a drummer named Jack Irons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Producers for Chris Cornell's Solo Album – Launchpad for Other Gigs
podcast.body: The group Eleven, comprising Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider, played a crucial role in producing Chris Cornell's debut solo record, *Euphoria Morning*. Their work on this album garnered them further producing gigs for notable artists like No Doubt and Josh Homme's Desert Session projects, connecting them to members of A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. "Chris reliant on both of them to help produce his debut solo record Euphoria Morning... who, based on this work, got producing gigs for no doubt in Josh Hommie in the early days of his desert session projects."

xref.title: Brian Potvin's Talent Scouting and Songwriting
xref.body: Upon the Pikes' retirement, guitarist Brian Potvin transitioned into talent scouting for Polygram and Universal Records, working with artists such as Finger Eleven and Tegan and Sara. He also freelances as a songwriter, contributing material to other bands and to the Discovery Channel, including the series "Survivor Man." "When the Pikes retired, he went to work scouting talent for Polygram, and later Universal Records. This had him work with everyone from finger 11 to Tegan and Sarah. He also freelances as a songwriter. Some material goes to other bands, while other stuff has been for the Discovery Channel, including the series Survivor Man."

xref.title: Expulsion from Peabody Institute
xref.body: Tori Amos studied classical music at the Peabody Institute until age eleven, at which point her discovery of rock music, including artists like Led Zeppelin and Jimi Hendrix, led to insubordination. Consequently, her scholarship was revoked, and she was asked to leave the institution. "Tori studied classical music at the Peabody until she was eleven, but then a problem. Tori discovered rock, zeppelin, jimmy Hendrix, and so on. And she became subordinate. Her scholarship was revoked, and she was asked to leave."

xref.title: Formed from Anthem – Early Origins
xref.body: The Red Hot Chili Peppers were formed by Flea and Hillel Slovak after their previous band, Anthem, broke up. Jack Irons, another musician connected to the Seattle scene through Eleven and Pearl Jam, later joined the Red Hot Chili Peppers for a period. "One was named Flea, and the other was Hillel Slovak, and when Anthem broke up, those two guys would form the Red Hot Chili Peppers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Henry Rollins – Former 7-Eleven Clerk from DC Replaced Co-Founder, Took Band to New Level
xref.body: Black Flag was co-founded in 1976 with Keith Morris as singer, but Morris was gone by 1979 (creative differences, cocaine and speed). After brief stints by Ron Reyes and Dez Cadena, the band discovered Henry Rollins — a Washington, D.C. hardcore fan and former 7-Eleven clerk — who had attended their shows. Rollins took Black Flag to an entirely new level and remained their singer until they broke up in summer 1986. "His replacement was a former 7-11 clerk from Washington, D.C., named Henry Rollins."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jack Irons' Collaboration – During Matt Cameron's Soundgarden Tenure
xref.body: Jack Irons, who was once a drummer for Eleven and briefly for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, worked with Pearl Jam at a time when Matt Cameron was performing with Soundgarden. Irons also played a crucial role in Eddie Vedder joining the band by passing along a demo tape. "Jack would later join the Red Hot Chili Peppers for a bit, and he worked with Pearl Jam when Matt Cameron went off with Soundgarden."
